findings.explanation: The new ajax_lookup route (sqladmin/application.py:519-537) is registered as a protected admin endpoint (Route '/{identity}/ajax/lookup') but is not decorated with @login_required, unlike every other admin route (index, list, details, delete, create, edit, export all carry @login_required at lines 340, 346, 371, 392, 409, 444, 483). It also performs no is_accessible/can_* authorization check on the resolved model_view, unlike the _export/_list/_details helpers (base lines 210-228) which raise 403 when model_view.is_accessible(request) is false. As a result, when an AuthenticationBackend is configured, an unauthenticated user can call /admin/{identity}/ajax/lookup?name=...&term=... and enumerate model data via loader.get_list(term), bypassing both authentication and per-view access control.

findings.suggested_fix: Bind the search term as a parameter instead of concatenating it into the SQL text. For example, build the pattern with a bound value: `cast(field, String).ilike(literal("%%%s%%" % term))` is still unsafe; instead use `cast(field, String).ilike(bindparam("term"))` with `stmt.bindparams(bindparam("term", value="%" + term + "%"))`, or use SQLAlchemy's `ilike` with a parameterized value such as `cast(field, String).ilike(f"%{term}%")` only if the ORM binds it — the safe approach is to pass the pattern as a bound parameter (e.g. `stmt.filter(or_(*[cast(f, String).ilike(bindparam("t")) for f in fields]).params(t="%" + term + "%"))`).

SQLadmin does not enforce any authentication to your application,

## AuthenticationBackend

SQLAdmin has a session-based authentication that will allow you
to integrate any existing authentication to it.

The class `AuthenticationBackend` has three methods you need to override:

* `authenticate`: Will be called for validating each incoming request.
* `login`: Will be called only in the login page to validate username/password.
* `logout`: Will be called only for the logout, usually clearin the session.

        form = await request.form()

        request.session.clear()
